title: Does counting in tens ever land on this number?
description: Counting in tens from ten builds a list of numbers on a strip, and the video looks for one hundred and twenty five on it. Every number on the list ends in zero, and Keeko's doubt, that a multiple of five must also be a multiple of ten, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: the multiples of ten are the numbers the count in tens lands on, and each ends in zero. Watch for students who think every multiple of five is also a multiple of ten.

source: List the multiples of 10 and say whether 125 is one of them.
video_script.why: The child lists the multiples of ten, sees that each ends in zero, and uses this to decide whether a number is on the list.
video_script.substitution: Count in tens from ten, write the list, and look for the number on it.
video_script.anchor: a strip of number cards counting in tens from 10, with the number 125 waiting beside it
video_script.wrong_answer: one hundred and twenty five is a multiple of ten
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says one hundred and twenty five is a multiple of ten because it is a multiple of five. Counting in tens from one hundred, the jumps land on one hundred and ten, twenty and thirty and miss it, so the bubble is struck through.
video_script.payoff_line: One hundred and twenty five is not a multiple of ten

final_answer.spoken: one hundred and twenty five is not a multiple of ten

maths_rules: the list goes from 120 to 130, so 125 is not on it
125 ends in 5, not 0, so 125 is not a multiple of 10
every multiple of 10 is a multiple of 5, but 125 = 5 x 25 is not 10 times a whole number
video_script.design: One idea: multiples of ten are the landing spots of the count in tens, and all end in zero. Assumes the child can skip count. Wrong idea: a multiple of five is a multiple of ten. The strip stays on the board to the end.

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to list the multiples of ten and say whether the number is one of them.

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step one, write the multiples of ten by counting in tens.
Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty, sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, one hundred.
<bookmark mark='next'/>Then one hundred and ten, one hundred and twenty, one hundred and thirty.

narration: <bookmark mark='zero'/>Step two, look at the last digit of every number on the list. Each one ends in zero.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, look for 125: the list goes from 120 to 130; 125 ends in 5, not 0

narration: <bookmark mark='gap'/>Step three, look for one hundred and twenty five on the list.
The list goes from one hundred and twenty to one hundred and thirty, and skips it.
<bookmark mark='five'/>One hundred and twenty five ends in five, not in zero.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 125 is not a multiple of 10, because it does not end in 0
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>One hundred and twenty five is not a multiple of ten, because it does not end in zero.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble: 125 is a multiple of 10 because it is a multiple of 5; jumps of 10 from 100 land on 110, 120, 130 and fly past 125; the bubble is struck through

marks.doubt: the bubble appears over the number 125
marks.why: 5 x 25 = 125 is written under the bubble
marks.jump: jumps of 10 from 100 land on 110, 120 and 130 and fly past 125

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks one hundred and twenty five is a multiple of ten.
<bookmark mark='why'/>Keeko says it is a multiple of five, so it must be one of ten as well.
<bookmark mark='jump'/>But count in tens from one hundred. The jumps land on one hundred and ten, one hundred and twenty, one hundred and thirty.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>Every multiple of ten is a multiple of five, but not the other way round.
